   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"></p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i></i></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2024-12-01_2025-11-29" name="us-gaap:InventoryPolicyTextBlock" id="c139161524" escape="true"><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i>Inventories</i></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">Inventories are recorded at cost as determined by the weighted-average cost method and are valued at the lower of cost or net realizable value.</p>
   <p style="background-color:#FFFFFF;font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"></p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i></i></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2024-12-01_2025-11-29" name="us-gaap:InvestmentPolicyTextBlock" id="c139161525" escape="true"><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><span style="color:#333333;"><i>Investments</i></span></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i>&#160;</i></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">Investments with a value of $<ix:nonFraction id="c139160691" contextRef="i_2025-11-29" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:CashSurrenderValueOfLifeInsurance" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-3">10,388</ix:nonFraction>&#160;and $<ix:nonFraction id="c139160692" contextRef="i_2024-11-30" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:CashSurrenderValueOfLifeInsurance" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-3">9,814</ix:nonFraction>&#160;represent the cash surrender value of life insurance contracts as of <em style="font: inherit;"> November 29, 2025 </em>and <em style="font: inherit;"> November 30, 2024</em>, respectively. These assets are held to primarily support supplemental pension plans and are recorded in other assets in the Consolidated Balance Sheets. The corresponding gain or loss associated with these contracts is reported in earnings each period as a component of selling, general and administrative expenses.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"></p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i></i></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2024-12-01_2025-11-29" name="us-gaap:EquitySecuritiesWithoutReadilyDeterminableFairValuePolicyTextBlock" id="c139161526" escape="true"><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i>Equity Investments</i></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i>&#160;</i></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">Investments in an entity where we own less than <em style="font: inherit;">20%</em> of the voting stock of the entity and do <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> exercise significant influence over operating and financial policies of the entity are accounted for using the measurement alternative at cost less impairment plus or minus observable price changes in orderly transactions. We have a policy in place to review our investments at least annually, to evaluate the accounting method and identify observable price changes that could indicate impairment. If we believe that an impairment exists, it is our policy to calculate the fair value of the investment and recognize as impairment any amount by which the carrying value exceeds the fair value of the investment. We recognized an impairment of $<ix:nonFraction id="c139160695" contextRef="d_2023-12-03_2024-11-30" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:EquitySecuritiesWithoutReadilyDeterminableFairValueImpairmentLossAnnualAmount" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-3">1,966</ix:nonFraction>&#160;for the year&#160;ended&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> November 30, 2024</em>. The book value of the equity investments was&#160;$<ix:nonFraction id="c139160696" contextRef="i_2025-11-29" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:EquitySecuritiesWithoutReadilyDeterminableFairValueAmount" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-3">3,574</ix:nonFraction> and&#160;$<ix:nonFraction id="c139160697" contextRef="i_2024-11-30" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:EquitySecuritiesWithoutReadilyDeterminableFairValueAmount" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-3">1,023</ix:nonFraction>&#160;as of&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> November 29, 2025</em>&#160;and&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> November 30, 2024</em>, respectively and are presented in Other assets in the&#160;Consolidated Balance Sheets.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"></p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i></i></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2024-12-01_2025-11-29" name="us-gaap:PropertyPlantAndEquipmentPolicyTextBlock" id="c139161527" escape="true"><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i>Property, Plant and Equipment</i></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i>&#160;</i></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">Property, plant and equipment are carried at cost and depreciated over the useful lives of the assets using the straight-line method. Estimated useful lives range from <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="i_2025-11-29_PropertyPlantAndEquipmentByTypeAxis-BuildingAndBuildingImprovementsMember_RangeAxis-MinimumMember" name="us-gaap:PropertyPlantAndEquipmentUsefulLife" id="c139160698" format="ixt-sec:duryear">20</ix:nonNumeric> to <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="i_2025-11-29_PropertyPlantAndEquipmentByTypeAxis-BuildingAndBuildingImprovementsMember_RangeAxis-MaximumMember" name="us-gaap:PropertyPlantAndEquipmentUsefulLife" id="c139160699" format="ixt-sec:duryear">40</ix:nonNumeric> years for buildings and improvements, <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="i_2025-11-29_PropertyPlantAndEquipmentByTypeAxis-MachineryAndEquipmentMember_RangeAxis-MinimumMember" name="us-gaap:PropertyPlantAndEquipmentUsefulLife" id="c139160700" format="ixt-sec:duryear">3</ix:nonNumeric> to <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="i_2025-11-29_PropertyPlantAndEquipmentByTypeAxis-MachineryAndEquipmentMember_RangeAxis-MaximumMember" name="us-gaap:PropertyPlantAndEquipmentUsefulLife" id="c139160701" format="ixt-sec:duryear">20</ix:nonNumeric> years for machinery and equipment, and the shorter of the lease or expected life for leasehold improvements. Fully depreciated assets are retained in property and accumulated depreciation accounts until disposed. Upon sale of an asset, the difference between the proceeds and remaining net book value is charged or credited to other&#160;(expense) income, net&#160;on the Consolidated Statements of Income. Expenditures that add value or extend the life of the respective assets are capitalized, while expenditures that are typical recurring repairs and maintenance are expensed as incurred. Interest costs associated with construction and implementation of property, plant and equipment of $<ix:nonFraction id="c139160702" contextRef="d_2024-12-01_2025-11-29" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:InterestCostsCapitalized" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-3">562</ix:nonFraction>, $<ix:nonFraction id="c139160703" contextRef="d_2023-12-03_2024-11-30" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:InterestCostsCapitalized" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-3">1,859</ix:nonFraction>&#160;and $<ix:nonFraction id="c139160704" contextRef="d_2022-12-04_2023-12-02" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:InterestCostsCapitalized" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-3">1,769</ix:nonFraction>&#160;were capitalized in <em style="font: inherit;">2025,</em> <em style="font: inherit;">2024</em> and <em style="font: inherit;">2023</em>, respectively.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"></p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i></i></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2024-12-01_2025-11-29" name="us-gaap:GoodwillAndIntangibleAssetsGoodwillPolicy" id="c139161528" escape="true"><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i>Goodwill</i></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i>&#160;</i></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">We evaluate our goodwill for impairment annually at the beginning of the <em style="font: inherit;">fourth</em> quarter or earlier upon the occurrence of substantive unfavorable changes in economic conditions, industry trends, costs, cash flows or ongoing declines in market capitalization. The quantitative impairment test requires judgment, including the identification of reporting units, the assignment of assets, liabilities and goodwill to reporting units, and the determination of fair value of each reporting unit. The impairment test requires the comparison of the fair value of each reporting unit with its carrying amount, including goodwill. In performing the impairment test, we determined the fair value of our reporting units through the income approach by using discounted cash flow (&#8220;DCF&#8221;) analyses. Determining fair value requires the Company to make judgments about appropriate discount rates, perpetual growth rates and the amount and timing of expected future cash flows. The cash flows employed in the DCF analysis for each reporting unit are based on the reporting unit's budget, long-term business plan and recent operating performance. Discount rate assumptions are based on an assessment of the risk inherent in the future cash flows of the respective reporting unit and market conditions. If the estimated fair value of a reporting unit exceeds its carrying value, goodwill is considered to <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> be impaired. If the carrying value exceeds estimated fair value, an impairment charge is recorded for any excess of the carrying value over the estimated fair value. Based on the analysis performed for our fiscal&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">2025</em> annual impairment test, there were <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> indications of impairment for any of our reporting units. See Note <em style="font: inherit;">5</em> for further information.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"></p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i></i></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2024-12-01_2025-11-29" name="us-gaap:GoodwillAndIntangibleAssetsIntangibleAssetsPolicy" id="c139161529" escape="true"><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i>Intangible Assets</i></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">Intangible assets include patents, customer lists, technology, trademarks and other intangible assets acquired from independent parties and are amortized on a straight-line basis with estimated useful lives ranging from <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="i_2025-11-29_RangeAxis-MinimumMember" name="us-gaap:FiniteLivedIntangibleAssetUsefulLife" id="c139160713" format="ixt-sec:duryear">2</ix:nonNumeric> to <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="i_2025-11-29_RangeAxis-MaximumMember" name="us-gaap:FiniteLivedIntangibleAssetUsefulLife" id="c139160714" format="ixt-sec:duryear">20</ix:nonNumeric> years. The straight-line method of amortization of these assets reflects an appropriate allocation of the costs of the intangible assets to earnings in proportion to the amount of economic benefits obtained in each reporting period.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"></p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i></i></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2024-12-01_2025-11-29" name="us-gaap:ImpairmentOrDisposalOfLongLivedAssetsPolicyTextBlock" id="c139161530" escape="true"><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i>Impairment of Long-Lived Assets</i></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i>&#160;</i></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">Our long-lived assets are tested for impairment whenever events or circumstances indicate that a carrying amount of an asset (asset group) <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em><em style="font: inherit;">not</em> be recoverable. An impairment loss would be measured and recognized when the carrying amount of an asset (asset group) exceeds the estimated undiscounted future cash flows expected to result from the use of the asset (asset group) and its eventual disposition. The impairment loss to be recorded would be the excess of the asset's carrying value over its fair value. Fair value is generally determined using a DCF analysis or other valuation technique. Costs related to internally developed intangible assets are expensed as incurred.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"></p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i></i></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2024-12-01_2025-11-29" name="us-gaap:ForeignCurrencyTransactionsAndTranslationsPolicyTextBlock" id="c139161531" escape="true"><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i>Foreign Currency Translation</i></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i>&#160;</i></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">Assets and liabilities of non-U.S. functional currency entities are translated to U.S. dollars at period-end exchange rates, and the resulting gains and losses arising from the translation of those net assets are recorded as a cumulative translation adjustment, a component of accumulated other comprehensive income (loss) in stockholders' equity. Revenues and expenses are translated using average exchange rates during the year. Foreign currency transaction gains and losses are included in other&#160;(expense) income, net&#160;in the Consolidated Statements of Income.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">We consider a subsidiary&#8217;s sales price drivers, currency denomination of sales transactions and inventory purchases to be the primary indicators in determining a foreign subsidiary&#8217;s functional currency. Our subsidiaries in certain European countries have a functional currency different than their local currency. All other foreign subsidiaries, which are located in North America, Latin America, Europe, India, the Middle East and Africa ("EIMEA") and Asia Pacific, have the same local and functional currency.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>

   <ix:exclude>&#160;</ix:exclude>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"></p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i></i></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2024-12-01_2025-11-29" name="us-gaap:PensionAndOtherPostretirementPlansPolicy" id="c139161532" escape="true"><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i>Pension and Other Postretirement Benefits</i></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b>&#160;</b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">We sponsor defined-benefit pension plans in both the U.S. and non-U.S. entities. Also in the U.S., we sponsor other postretirement plans for health care and life insurance benefits. Expenses and liabilities for the pension plans and other postretirement plans are actuarially calculated. These calculations are based on our assumptions related to the discount rate, expected return on assets, projected salary increases, health care cost trend rates and mortality rates. The discount rate assumption is determined using an actuarial yield curve approach, which results in a discount rate that reflects the characteristics of the plan. The approach identifies a broad population of corporate bonds that meet the quality and size criteria for the particular plan. We use this approach rather than a specific index that has a certain set of bonds that <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>or <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em><em style="font: inherit;">not</em> be representative of the characteristics of our particular plan. Our expected long-term rate of return on U.S. plan assets was based on our target asset allocation assumption of <ix:nonFraction id="c139160718" contextRef="i_2025-11-29_DefinedBenefitPlanByPlanAssetCategoriesAxis-DefinedBenefitPlanEquitySecuritiesMember" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:DefinedBenefitPlanPlanAssetsTargetAllocationPercentage" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="2">55</ix:nonFraction> percent equities and <ix:nonFraction id="c139160719" contextRef="i_2025-11-29_DefinedBenefitPlanByPlanAssetCategoriesAxis-FixedIncomeFundsMember" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:DefinedBenefitPlanPlanAssetsTargetAllocationPercentage" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="2">45</ix:nonFraction> percent fixed income. Management, in conjunction with our external financial advisors, determines the expected long-term rate of return on plan assets by considering the expected future returns and volatility levels for each asset class that are based on historical returns and forward-looking observations. The expected long-term rate of return on plan assets assumption used in each non-U.S. plan is determined on a plan-by-plan basis for each local jurisdiction and is based on expected future returns for the investment mix of assets currently in the portfolio for that plan.&#160;Management, in conjunction with our external financial advisors, develops expected rates of return for each plan, considers expected long-term returns for each asset category in the plan, reviews expectations for inflation for each local jurisdiction, and estimates the impact of active management of the plan&#8217;s assets. Note <em style="font: inherit;">10</em> includes disclosure of assumptions employed in these measurements for both the non-U.S. and U.S. plans.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"></p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i></i></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2024-12-01_2025-11-29" name="us-gaap:AssetRetirementObligationsPolicy" id="c139161533" escape="true"><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i>Asset Retirement Obligations</i></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b>&#160;</b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">We recognize asset retirement obligations ("ARO") in the period in which we have an existing legal obligation associated with the retirement of a tangible long-lived asset, and the amount can be reasonably estimated. The ARO is recognized at fair value when the liability is incurred. Upon initial recognition of a liability, that cost is capitalized as part of the related long-lived asset and accreted on a straight-line basis over the remaining estimated useful life of the related asset. We have recognized a liability related to special handling of asbestos related materials in certain facilities for which we have plans or expectation of plans to undertake a major renovation or demolition project that would require the removal of asbestos or have plans or expectation of plans to exit a facility. In addition, we have determined that we have facilities with some level of asbestos that will require abatement action in the future. Once the probability and timeframe of an action are determined, we apply certain assumptions to determine the related liability and asset. These assumptions include the use of inflation rates, the use of credit adjusted risk-free discount rates and the estimation of costs to handle asbestos related materials. The recorded liability is required to be adjusted for changes resulting from the passage of time and/or revisions to the timing or the amount of the original estimate. The asset retirement obligation liability was&#160;$<ix:nonFraction id="c139160721" contextRef="i_2025-11-29" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:AssetRetirementObligationsNoncurrent" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-3">3,155</ix:nonFraction>&#160;and $<ix:nonFraction id="c139160722" contextRef="i_2024-11-30" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:AssetRetirementObligationsNoncurrent" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-3">3,321</ix:nonFraction>&#160;at <em style="font: inherit;"> November 29, 2025 </em>and <em style="font: inherit;"> November 30, 2024</em>, respectively.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"></p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i></i></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2024-12-01_2025-11-29" name="us-gaap:EnvironmentalCostsPolicy" id="c139161534" escape="true"><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i>Environmental Costs</i></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i>&#160;</i></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">Environmental expenditures that relate to current operations are expensed or capitalized as appropriate. Expenditures that relate to an existing condition caused by past operations, and which do <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> contribute to current or future revenue generation, are expensed. Liabilities are recorded when environmental assessments are made, or remedial efforts are probable, and the costs can be reasonably estimated. The timing of these accruals is generally <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> later than the completion of feasibility studies.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"></p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i></i></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2024-12-01_2025-11-29" name="us-gaap:CommitmentsAndContingenciesPolicyTextBlock" id="c139161535" escape="true"><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i>Contingent Consideration Liabilities</i></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b>&#160;</b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">Concurrent with business acquisitions, we enter into agreements that require us to pay the sellers a certain amount based upon a formula related to the entity&#8217;s financial results. The change in fair value of the contingent consideration liability is recorded in SG&amp;A expenses in the Consolidated Statements of Income.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"></p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i></i></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2024-12-01_2025-11-29" name="us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensationOptionAndIncentivePlansPolicy" id="c139161536" escape="true"><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i>Share-based Compensation</i></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i>&#160;</i></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">We have various share-based compensation programs which provide for equity awards, including non-qualified stock options, incentive stock options, restricted stock units, performance awards and deferred compensation. We use the straight-line attribution method to recognize compensation expense associated with share-based awards based on the fair value on the date of grant, net of the estimated forfeiture rate. Expense is recognized over the requisite service period related to each award, which is the period between the grant date and the earlier of the award&#8217;s stated vesting term or the date the employee is eligible for early retirement based on the terms of the plan. The fair value of stock options is estimated using the Black-Scholes option pricing model. All of our stock compensation expense is recorded in SG&amp;A expenses in the Consolidated Statements of Income.<b> </b>See Note <em style="font: inherit;">9</em> for additional information.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b>&#160;</b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"></p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i></i></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2024-12-01_2025-11-29" name="us-gaap:EarningsPerSharePolicyTextBlock" id="c139161537" escape="true"><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i>Earnings per Share</i></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b>&#160;</b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">Basic earnings per share is calculated by dividing net income attributable to H.B. Fuller by the weighted-average number of common shares outstanding during the applicable period. Diluted earnings per share is based upon the weighted-average number of common and common equivalent shares outstanding during the applicable period. The difference between basic and diluted earnings per share is attributable to share-based compensation awards. We use the treasury stock method to calculate the effect of outstanding awards, which computes total employee proceeds as the sum of (a) the amount the employee must pay upon exercise of the award and (b) the amount of unearned share-based compensation costs attributed to future services. Share-based compensation awards for which total employee proceeds exceed the average market price over the applicable period have an antidilutive effect on earnings per share, and accordingly, are excluded from the calculation of diluted earnings per share. The computations for basic and diluted earnings per share are as follows:</p>

   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"></p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i></i></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2024-12-01_2025-11-29" name="us-gaap:DerivativesPolicyTextBlock" id="c139161538" escape="true"><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i>Financial Instruments and Derivatives</i></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b>&#160;</b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">As a part of our ongoing operations, we are exposed to market risks such as changes in foreign currency exchange rates and interest rates. To manage these risks, we <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>enter into derivative transactions pursuant to our established policies.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">Our objective is to balance, where possible, non-functional currency denominated assets to non-functional currency denominated liabilities to have a natural hedge and minimize foreign exchange impacts. We minimize risks from foreign currency exchange rate fluctuations through normal operating and financing activities and, when deemed appropriate, through the use of derivative instruments. Derivatives consisted primarily of forward currency contracts used to manage foreign currency denominated assets and liabilities. For derivative instruments outstanding that were <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> designated as hedges for accounting purposes, the gains and losses related to mark-to-market adjustments were recognized as other&#160;(expense) income, net&#160;in the income statement during the periods the derivative instruments were outstanding. To manage exposure to currency rate movements on expected cash flows, the Company <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>enter into cross-currency swap agreements.&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">The Company manages interest expense using a mix of fixed and floating rate debt. &#160;To manage exposure to interest rate movements and to reduce borrowing costs, the Company <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>enter into interest rate swap agreements.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">Changes in the fair values of derivatives are recorded in net earnings or other comprehensive income, based on the type of derivative, and whether the instrument is designated and effective as a hedge transaction. Gains or losses on derivative instruments reported in accumulated other comprehensive income (loss) are reclassified to earnings in the period the hedged item affects earnings. Any ineffectiveness is recognized in earnings in the current period. We maintain master netting arrangements that allow us to net settle contracts with the same counterparties; we do <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> elect to offset amounts in our Consolidated Balance Sheet.&#160; These arrangements generally do <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> call for collateral. We do <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> enter into any speculative positions with regard to derivative instruments. See Note <em style="font: inherit;">12</em> for further information regarding our financial instruments.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b>&#160;</b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"></p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i></i></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2024-12-01_2025-11-29" name="ful:PurchaseOfCompanyCommonStockPolicyTextBlock" id="c139161539" escape="true"><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i>Purchase of Company Common Stock</i></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b>&#160;</b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">Under the Minnesota Business Corporation Act, repurchased stock is included in authorized shares&#160;but is <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> included in shares outstanding. The excess of the repurchase cost over par value is charged to additional paid-in capital. When additional paid-in capital is exhausted, the excess reduces retained earnings. We indirectly repurchased <ix:nonFraction id="c139160739" contextRef="d_2024-12-01_2025-11-29" unitRef="Share" name="us-gaap:SharesPaidForTaxWithholdingForShareBasedCompensation" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">56,228</ix:nonFraction>, <ix:nonFraction id="c139160740" contextRef="d_2023-12-03_2024-11-30" unitRef="Share" name="us-gaap:SharesPaidForTaxWithholdingForShareBasedCompensation" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">93,102</ix:nonFraction>&#160;and <ix:nonFraction id="c139160741" contextRef="d_2022-12-04_2023-12-02" unitRef="Share" name="us-gaap:SharesPaidForTaxWithholdingForShareBasedCompensation" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">113,868</ix:nonFraction>&#160;shares of common stock in <em style="font: inherit;">2025,</em> <em style="font: inherit;">2024</em> and <em style="font: inherit;">2023</em>, respectively, through a net-settlement feature in connection with the statutory minimum tax withholding related to vesting of restricted stock. We repurchased <ix:nonFraction id="c139160745" contextRef="d_2024-12-01_2025-11-29" unitRef="Share" name="us-gaap:StockRepurchasedDuringPeriodShares" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">977,537</ix:nonFraction> shares and <ix:nonFraction id="c139160746" contextRef="d_2023-12-03_2024-11-30" unitRef="Share" name="us-gaap:StockRepurchasedDuringPeriodShares" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">407,400</ix:nonFraction>&#160;shares of common stock from our share repurchase program in <em style="font: inherit;">2025</em> and <em style="font: inherit;">2024,</em> respectively. <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c139160749">No</span> shares were repurchased from our share repurchase program in <em style="font: inherit;">2023.</em></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"></p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i></i></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2024-12-01_2025-11-29" name="ful:SupplierFinanceProgramPolicyPolicyTextBlock" id="c139161540" escape="true"><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i><span style="background-color:#ffffff;">Supplier Finance Program</span></i></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">We have&#160;agreements with&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">third</em>&#160;parties&#160;to provide&#160;supplier finance programs which facilitate&#160;participating suppliers' ability to finance payment obligations of the Company with designated&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">third</em>-party financial institutions. Participating suppliers&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> may,&#160;</em>at their sole discretion, elect to finance&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">one</em>&#160;or more payment obligations of the Company prior to their scheduled due dates at a discounted price to participating financial institutions. The Company has&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">no</em>&#160;economic interest in the sale of these suppliers&#8217; receivables and&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">no</em>&#160;direct financial relationship with the financial institutions concerning these services. The Company&#8217;s obligations to its suppliers, including amounts due and scheduled payment dates, are&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">not</em>&#160;impacted by suppliers&#8217; decisions to finance amounts under these arrangements. The outstanding payment obligations that were confirmed as valid and remained outstanding as of&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> November 29, 2025</em> were appro<span style="background-color:#ffffff;">ximately $<ix:nonFraction id="c139160757" contextRef="i_2025-11-29" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:SupplierFinanceProgramObligation" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-3">7,379</ix:nonFraction></span><b><span style="background-color:#ffffff;">.</span></b> These obligations under the Company&#8217;s supplier finance programs are included in <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c139161421">Accounts Payable</span> in the Consolidated Balance Sheets, and the associated payments are reflected in the cash flows from operating activities section of the Consolidated Statements of Cash Flows.</p>

   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"></p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><i></i></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2024-12-01_2025-11-29" name="ful:BusinessInterruptionInsurancePolicyTextBlock" id="c139161541" escape="true"><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><i>Business&#160;Interruption Insurance Proceeds</i></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">The Company made insurance claims to recover lost margin and additional costs incurred in connection with a fire at our Tucker production facility in <em style="font: inherit;"> June 2022 </em>and unprecedented freezing weather that impacted our Texas facilities in <em style="font: inherit;"> February 2021. </em>During the year ended <em style="font: inherit;"> November 30, 2024, </em>the Company received business interruption insurance recovery payments of $<ix:nonFraction id="c139160758" contextRef="d_2023-12-03_2024-11-30_BusinessInterruptionLossAxis-FireAndFreezingWeatherClaimsMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:ProceedsFromInsuranceSettlementInvestingActivities" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-3">2,393</ix:nonFraction>, which have been recorded in selling, general and administrative expenses. The insurance claims were fully settled in <em style="font: inherit;"> September 2024. </em>We did <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> receive any insurance recovery payments in <em style="font: inherit;">2025.</em></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"></p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i></i></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2024-12-01_2025-11-29" name="us-gaap:NewAccountingPronouncementsPolicyPolicyTextBlock" id="c139161542" escape="true"><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i>New Accounting Pronouncements</i></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">In <em style="font: inherit;"> November 2024, </em>the FASB&#160;issued Accounting Standards Update ("ASU") <em style="font: inherit;">No.</em> <em style="font: inherit;">2024</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">03,</em> <i>Income Statement - Reporting Comprehensive Income - Expense Disaggregation Disclosures (Subtopic <em style="font: inherit;">220</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">40</em>): Disaggregation of Income Statement Expenses</i>, which requires additional disclosure of the nature of expenses included in our Consolidated Financial Statements. Our effective date of this ASU is our fiscal year ending <em style="font: inherit;"> December 2, 2028. </em>We are currently evaluating the impact of adopting this guidance on the related financial statement disclosures.&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">In <em style="font: inherit;"> December 2023, </em>the FASB issued ASU <em style="font: inherit;">No.</em> <em style="font: inherit;">2023</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">09,</em> <i>Income Taxes (Topic <em style="font: inherit;">740</em>): Improvements to Income Tax Disclosures</i>. This ASU requires entities to provide additional information in the rate reconciliation and additional disclosures about income taxes paid. This guidance requires public entities to disclose in their rate reconciliation table additional categories of information about federal, state, and foreign income taxes and to provide more details about the reconciling items in some categories if the items meet a quantitative threshold. Our effective date of this ASU is our fiscal year ending <em style="font: inherit;"> November 28, 2026. </em>We are currently evaluating the impact of adopting this guidance on the related financial statement disclosures.&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>

   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">In <em style="font: inherit;"> November 2023, </em>the FASB issued ASU&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">No.</em> <em style="font: inherit;">2023</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">07,</em> <i>Segment Reporting (Topic <em style="font: inherit;">280</em>): Improvements to Reportable Segment Disclosures.</i> This ASU requires enhanced disclosures regarding significant segment expenses and other segment items. The guidance requires public entities to provide in interim periods all disclosures about a reportable segment's profit or loss and assets that are currently required annually. We adopted the standard retrospectively beginning with our fiscal year ending <em style="font: inherit;"> November 29, 2025. </em>Refer to Note <em style="font: inherit;">15,</em> <i>Segments</i>, for further information on our segment reporting. &#160;</p>

   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">On <em style="font: inherit;"> May 20, 2024, </em>we acquired the assets of ND Industries,&#160;Inc.&#160;(&#8220;ND Industries&#8221;) for a base purchase price of $<ix:nonFraction id="c139160816" contextRef="d_2024-05-20_2024-05-20_BusinessAcquisitionAxis-NdIndustriesMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:BusinessCombinationConsiderationTransferred1" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-3">254,037</ix:nonFraction> which was funded through borrowings on our credit facility and existing cash.    <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b>Note </b><b><em style="font: inherit;">3:</em></b><b> Restructuring Actions </b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">During fiscal year&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">2023</em><i>,</i>&#160;the Company&#160;approved&#160;restructuring plans (the "Plans")&#160;related to&#160;organizational changes and other actions to optimize operations and integrate acquired businesses. The Plans began to be implemented in the&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">second</em>&#160;quarter of fiscal year&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">2023</em>&#160;and were completed as of <em style="font: inherit;"> November 29, 2025. </em>Remaining cash payments will continue into fiscal year <em style="font: inherit;">2026.</em> In implementing the Plans, the Company currently expects to incur pre-tax costs of approximately $<ix:nonFraction id="c139160838" contextRef="i_2025-11-29_RestructuringCostAndReserveAxis-EmployeeSeveranceMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:RestructuringAndRelatedCostExpectedCost1" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-7">80,000</ix:nonFraction>&#160;to <span style="background-color:#ffffff;">$<ix:nonFraction id="c139160839" contextRef="i_2025-11-29_RestructuringCostAndReserveAxis-OtherRestructuringMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:RestructuringAndRelatedCostExpectedCost1" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-6">85,000</ix:nonFraction></span>&#160;for severance and related employee costs globally, and other restructuring costs related to the streamlining of processes and the payment of anticipated income taxes in certain jurisdictions related to the Plans.</p>

   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b>Note <em style="font: inherit;">6:</em> Leases</b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">As a lessee, the Company leases office, manufacturing and warehouse space, and equipment. Certain lease agreements include rental payments adjusted annually based on changes in an inflation index. Our leases do <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> contain material residual value guarantees or material restrictive covenants. Lease expense is recognized on a straight-line basis over the lease term. We determine if an arrangement is a lease upon inception. A contract is or contains a lease if the contract conveys the right to control the use of an identified asset for a period of time in exchange for consideration. The right to control the use of an asset includes the right to obtain substantially all of the economic benefits of the underlying asset and the right to direct how and for what purpose the asset is used.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">Operating lease and finance lease right-of-use assets and liabilities are recognized at commencement date based on the present value of lease payments over the lease term. The discount rate used to calculate present value is the Company&#8217;s incremental borrowing rate. We determine the incremental borrowing rate for each lease based primarily on its lease term and the economic environment of the applicable country or region.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">Certain leases include <em style="font: inherit;">one</em> or more options to renew, with terms that can extend the lease term up to <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c139160873">five</span> years. We include options to renew the lease as part of the right-of-use lease asset and liability when it is reasonably certain we will exercise the option. In addition, certain leases contain termination options with an associated penalty. In general, the Company is <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> reasonably certain to exercise such options.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">For the measurement and classification of lease agreements, we group lease and non-lease components into a single lease component for all underlying asset classes. Variable lease payments primarily include payments for non-lease components, such as maintenance costs, payments for leased assets used beyond their non-cancelable lease term as adjusted for contractual options to terminate or renew, and payments for non-components such as sales tax. Certain leases contain immaterial variable lease payments based on usage.</p>
   <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&#160;</p>

   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">We did <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c139160881">not</span> have any outstanding notes payable balance at&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> November 29, 2025</em>&#160;and a balance of&#160;$<ix:nonFraction id="c139160882" contextRef="i_2024-11-30" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:NotesPayableCurrent" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-3">587</ix:nonFraction>&#160;at&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> November 30, 2024</em>. Notes payable&#160;primarily represents various foreign subsidiaries&#8217; other short-term borrowings that were <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> part of committed lines. The weighted-average interest rate&#160;on short-term borrowings outstanding was&#160;<ix:nonFraction id="c139160884" contextRef="i_2025-11-29" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:ShortTermDebtWeightedAverageInterestRate" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="4">1.35</ix:nonFraction> percent in&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">2024</em>.&#160;Fair values of these short-term obligations approximate their carrying values due to their short maturity. There were <ix:nonFraction id="c139160886" contextRef="i_2025-11-29_CreditFacilityAxis-RevolvingCreditFacilityMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:LinesOfCreditCurrent" scale="3" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen" decimals="-3">no</ix:nonFraction> funds drawn from the short-term committed lines at <em style="font: inherit;"> November 29, 2025</em>.</p>

The&#160;Revolving Credit Facility matures on <em style="font: inherit;"> February 15, 2028.&#160;</em></p>

   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i>Covenants and Other</i></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">Under the <span style="color:#000000">Refinancing and Incremental Amendment</span>, the Revolving Credit Facility and Term Loan A are subject to certain covenants and restrictions.&#160;For these facilities, we are required to maintain a secured leverage ratio, as defined in the agreement, <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> greater than <ix:nonFraction id="c139160974" contextRef="d_2023-02-15_2023-02-15_CreditFacilityAxis-RevolvingCreditFacilityMember" unitRef="Pure" name="ful:DebtInstrumentCovenantSecuredLeverageRatioForFiscalQuartersEndingOnOrPriorToJune12024" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">4.75</ix:nonFraction> to <em style="font: inherit;">1.00</em> for our fiscal quarters ending&#160;on or prior to <em style="font: inherit;"> June 1, 2024 </em>and then <ix:nonFraction id="c139160976" contextRef="d_2023-02-15_2023-02-15_CreditFacilityAxis-RevolvingCreditFacilityMember" unitRef="Pure" name="ful:DebtInstrumentCovenantSecuredLeverageRatioForFiscalQuartersEndingAfterJune12024" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">4.50</ix:nonFraction> to <em style="font: inherit;">1.00</em> thereafter. We are also required to maintain an interest coverage ratio of <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> less than <ix:nonFraction id="c139160979" contextRef="d_2023-02-15_2023-02-15_CreditFacilityAxis-RevolvingCreditFacilityMember" unitRef="Pure" name="ful:DebtInstrumentCovenantInterestCoverageRatio" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">2.00</ix:nonFraction> to <em style="font: inherit;">1.00.</em>&#160;</p>

   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">Restrictive covenants include, but are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> limited to, limitations on secured and unsecured borrowings, interest coverage, intercompany transfers and&#160;investments, <em style="font: inherit;">third</em> party investments, dispositions of assets, leases, liens, dividends and distributions, and contains a maximum total debt to trailing <em style="font: inherit;">twelve</em>&#160;months EBITDA requirement. Certain covenants become less restrictive after meeting leverage or other financial ratios. In addition, we cannot be a member of&#160;any consolidated group as defined for income tax purposes other than with our subsidiaries.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><br/> We are subject to mandatory prepayments in the <em style="font: inherit;">first</em> quarter of each fiscal year equal to <ix:nonFraction id="c139160985" contextRef="d_2023-02-15_2023-02-15_DebtInstrumentAxis-SecondAmendedAndRestatedCreditAgreementMember" unitRef="Pure" name="ful:DebtInstrumentMandatoryPrepaymentsOfExcessCashflowPercentage" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="1">50</ix:nonFraction> percent of Excess Cash Flow, as defined in&#160;<span style="color:#000000">the Refinancing and Incremental Amendment</span>, of the prior fiscal year less any voluntary prepayments made during that fiscal year. The Excess Cash Flow Percentage shall be&#160;reduced to <ix:nonFraction id="c139160986" contextRef="d_2023-02-15_2023-02-15_DebtInstrumentAxis-SecondAmendedAndRestatedCreditAgreementMember" unitRef="Pure" name="ful:DebtInstrumentMandatoryPrepaymentsOfExcessCashflowWhenSecuredLeverageRatioIsBelow425Percentage" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="2">25</ix:nonFraction> percent when our Secured Leverage Ratio is below <em style="font: inherit;">4.25:1.00</em> and to <ix:nonFraction id="c139160988" contextRef="d_2023-02-15_2023-02-15_DebtInstrumentAxis-SecondAmendedAndRestatedCreditAgreementMember" unitRef="Pure" name="ful:DebtInstrumentMandatoryPrepaymentsOfExcessCashflowWhenSecuredLeverageRatioIsBelow375Percentage" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-3">0</ix:nonFraction> percent when our Secured Leverage Ratio is below <em style="font: inherit;">3.75:1.00.</em></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>

   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">The Indenture under which the Public Notes have been issued contains covenants imposing certain limitations on the ability of the Company to incur liens or enter into sales and leaseback transactions. It also provides for customary events of default (subject in certain cases to customary grace and cure periods), which include among other things nonpayment, breach of covenants in the Indenture and certain events of bankruptcy and insolvency. If an event of default occurs and is continuing with respect to the Public Notes, the Trustee or holders of at least <em style="font: inherit;">25%</em> in principal amount outstanding of the Public Notes <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>declare the principal and the accrued and unpaid interest, if any, on all of the outstanding Public Notes to be due and payable. These covenants and events of default are subject to a number of important qualifications, limitations and exceptions that are described in the Indenture.</p>

  <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2024-12-01_2025-11-29" name="us-gaap:DisclosureOfCompensationRelatedCostsShareBasedPaymentsTextBlock" id="c3086989" escape="true">
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><span style="color:#333333;"><b>Note <em style="font: inherit;">9:</em> Accounting for Share-Based Compensation</b></span></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><span style="color:#ff0000;"><b>&#160;</b></span></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i>Overview</i></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b>&#160;</b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">We have various share-based compensation programs, which provide for equity awards including non-qualified stock options, incentive stock options, restricted stock units, performance awards and deferred compensation. These equity awards fall under several plans and are described below.</p>
   <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i>Share-based Compensation Plans</i></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">We currently grant stock options and restricted stock units under equity compensation and deferred compensation plans.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">Stock options are granted to officers and key employees at prices <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> less than the fair market value at the date of grant. Non-qualified stock options are generally exercisable beginning <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c139161020">one</span> year from the date of grant in cumulative yearly amounts of <ix:nonFraction id="c139161021" contextRef="d_2024-12-01_2025-11-29_AwardTypeAxis-EmployeeStockOptionMember_VestingAxis-ShareBasedCompensationAwardTrancheOneMember" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:SharebasedCompensationArrangementBySharebasedPaymentAwardAwardVestingRightsPercentage" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="3">33.3</ix:nonFraction> percent. Incentive stock options are based on certain performance-based criteria and are generally exercisable at a stated date when the performance criteria is measured. Stock options generally have a contractual term of <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2024-12-01_2025-11-29_AwardTypeAxis-EmployeeStockOptionMember_VestingAxis-ShareBasedCompensationAwardTrancheOneMember" name="us-gaap:SharebasedCompensationArrangementBySharebasedPaymentAwardExpirationPeriod" id="c139161022" format="ixt-sec:duryear">10</ix:nonNumeric> years. Options exercised represent newly issued shares.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">Restricted stock awards are nonvested stock-based awards that include grants of restricted stock units. Restricted stock awards are independent of option grants and are subject to forfeiture if employment terminates prior to the release of the restrictions. Time-based restricted stock awards generally vest beginning <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c139161023">one</span> year from the date of grant or <ix:nonFraction id="c139161024" contextRef="d_2024-12-01_2025-11-29_AwardTypeAxis-RestrictedStockMember_VestingAxis-ShareBasedCompensationAwardTrancheOneMember" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:SharebasedCompensationArrangementBySharebasedPaymentAwardAwardVestingRightsPercentage" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="3">33.3</ix:nonFraction> percent per year for <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c139161025">three</span> years, depending on the grant. Performance-based restricted stock awards vest <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c139161026">three</span> years from the date of grant. During the vesting period, ownership of the shares cannot be transferred.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">Restricted stock units have dividend equivalent rights equal to the cash dividend paid on restricted stock shares. However, restricted stock units do <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> have voting rights of common stock and are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> considered issued and outstanding upon grant. Restricted stock units become newly issued shares when vested. The dividend equivalent rights for restricted stock units are forfeitable.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">We expense the cost, which is the grant date fair market value, of the restricted stock units ratably over the period during which the restrictions lapse. The grant date fair value is our closing stock price on the date of grant.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt;">&#160;</p>

       <em style="font: inherit;">50</em>

   <ix:exclude>&#160;</ix:exclude>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">We are required to recognize compensation expense when an employee is eligible to retire. We consider employees eligible to retire at age <em style="font: inherit;">55</em> and after <em style="font: inherit;">10</em> years of service. Awards granted to retirement-eligible employees are forfeited if the retirement-eligible employees retire prior to <em style="font: inherit;">180</em> days after the grant. Accordingly, the related compensation expense is recognized during the <em style="font: inherit;">180</em> day period for awards granted to retirement-eligible employees or over the period from the grant date to the date retirement eligibility is achieved, if less than the stated vesting period.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i><em style="font: inherit;">2020</em> Master Incentive Plan</i></p>

The plan permits granting of (a) stock options; (b) stock appreciation rights; (c) restricted stock and restricted stock units; (d) performance awards; (e) dividend equivalents; (f) other awards based on our common stock, including shares for amounts employees or non-employee directors deferred under the deferred compensation plans.    </ix:nonNumeric>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">Expected life &#8211; We use historical employee exercise and option expiration data to estimate the expected life assumption for the Black-Scholes grant-date valuation. We believe that this historical data is currently the best estimate of the expected term of a new option. We use a weighted-average expected life for all awards.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">Expected volatility &#8211; Volatility is calculated using our stock&#8217;s historical volatility for the same period of time as the expected life. We have <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> reason to believe that its future volatility will differ from the past.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">Risk-free interest rate &#8211; The rate is based on the U.S. Treasury yield curve in effect at the time of the grant for the same period of time as the expected life.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">Expected dividend yield &#8211; The calculation is based on the total expected annual dividend payout divided by the closing stock price on the date of grant.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>

   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i>Expense</i></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">We use the straight-line attribution method to recognize share-based compensation expense for option awards and restricted stock units. Incentive stock options and performance awards are based on certain performance-based metrics and the expense is adjusted quarterly, based on our projections of the achievement of those metrics. The amount of share-based compensation expense recognized during a period is based on the value of the portion of the awards that are ultimately expected to vest. The expense is recognized over the requisite service period, which for us is the period between the grant date and the earlier of the award&#8217;s stated vesting term or the date the employee is eligible for early vesting based on the terms of the plans.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>

All share-based compensation was recorded as SG&amp;A expense.</p>
   <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><span style="background-color:#ffffff;">As of </span><em style="font: inherit;"> November 29, 2025</em><span style="background-color:#ffffff;">, </span>$<ix:nonFraction id="c139161052" contextRef="i_2025-11-29_AwardTypeAxis-EmployeeStockOptionMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:EmployeeServiceShareBasedCompensationNonvestedAwardsTotalCompensationCostNotYetRecognized" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-3">9,891</ix:nonFraction><span style="background-color:#ffffff;">&#160;of unrecognized compensation costs related to unvested stock option awards is expected to be recognized over a weighted-average period of </span><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2024-12-01_2025-11-29_AwardTypeAxis-EmployeeStockOptionMember" name="us-gaap:EmployeeServiceShareBasedCompensationNonvestedAwardsTotalCompensationCostNotYetRecognizedPeriodForRecognition1" id="c139161053" format="ixt-sec:duryear">1.1</ix:nonNumeric><span style="background-color:#ffffff;">&#160;years.    <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b>Note <em style="font: inherit;">10:</em> Pension and Postretirement Benefits&#160;</b></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b>Defined Contribution Plan</b></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">All U.S. employees have the option of contributing up to <ix:nonFraction id="c139161128" contextRef="d_2024-12-01_2025-11-29" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:DefinedContributionPlanMaximumAnnualContributionsPerEmployeePercent" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="2">75</ix:nonFraction> percent of their pre-tax earnings to a <em style="font: inherit;">401</em>(k) plan, subject to IRS limitations. We match up to the <em style="font: inherit;">first</em> <ix:nonFraction id="c139161131" contextRef="d_2024-12-01_2025-11-29" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:DefinedContributionPlanEmployerMatchingContributionPercent" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="2">4</ix:nonFraction> percent of each employee's pre-tax earnings, based on the employee&#8217;s contributions. All U.S. employees are eligible for a separate annual non-discretionary retirement contribution to the <em style="font: inherit;">401</em>(k) plan of <ix:nonFraction id="c139161133" contextRef="d_2024-12-01_2025-11-29" unitRef="Pure" name="ful:DefinedContributionPlanAnnualRetirementPercentage" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="2">1</ix:nonFraction> percent of pay, that is invested based on the election of the individual participant. The <ix:nonFraction id="c139161134" contextRef="d_2024-12-01_2025-11-29" unitRef="Pure" name="ful:DefinedContributionPlanAnnualRetirementPercentage" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="2">1</ix:nonFraction> percent contribution is in addition to our <ix:nonFraction id="c139161135" contextRef="d_2024-12-01_2025-11-29" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:DefinedContributionPlanEmployerMatchingContributionPercent" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="2">4</ix:nonFraction> percent matching contribution described above and is in lieu of participation in our defined benefit pension plan. The total contribution to the <em style="font: inherit;">401</em>(k) plan for&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">2025</em> was $<ix:nonFraction id="c139161138" contextRef="d_2024-12-01_2025-11-29" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DefinedContributionPlanCostRecognized" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-3">16,537</ix:nonFraction> which included the cost of the <ix:nonFraction id="c139161139" contextRef="d_2024-12-01_2025-11-29" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:DefinedContributionPlanEmployerMatchingContributionPercent" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="2">4</ix:nonFraction> percent company match of $<ix:nonFraction id="c139161140" contextRef="d_2024-12-01_2025-11-29_RetirementPlanTypeAxis-FourPercentMatchMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DefinedContributionPlanCostRecognized" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-3">10,389</ix:nonFraction> and the additional <ix:nonFraction id="c139161141" contextRef="d_2024-12-01_2025-11-29" unitRef="Pure" name="ful:DefinedContributionPlanAnnualRetirementPercentage" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="2">1</ix:nonFraction> percent contribution of<span style="background-color:#ffffff;"> $<ix:nonFraction id="c139161142" contextRef="d_2024-12-01_2025-11-29_RetirementPlanTypeAxis-OnePercentMatchMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DefinedContributionPlanCostRecognized" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-3">6,148</ix:nonFraction>. T</span>he total contributions to the <em style="font: inherit;">401</em>(k) plan were $<ix:nonFraction id="c139161144" contextRef="d_2023-12-03_2024-11-30" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DefinedContributionPlanCostRecognized" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-4">15,590</ix:nonFraction> and $<ix:nonFraction id="c139161145" contextRef="d_2022-12-04_2023-12-02" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DefinedContributionPlanCostRecognized" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-3">14,221</ix:nonFraction> in&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">2024</em> and <em style="font: inherit;">2023</em>, respectively.</p>
   <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">All U.S. employees are eligible to receive an annual discretionary non-elective contribution to the <em style="font: inherit;">401</em>(k) plan of up to <em style="font: inherit;">3</em> percent based on achieving the Company&#8217;s earnings per share target. This discretionary contribution is in addition to the contributions described above. There was $<ix:nonFraction id="c139161150" contextRef="d_2024-12-01_2025-11-29" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DefinedContributionPlanEmployerDiscretionaryContributionAmount" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-3">2,819</ix:nonFraction> accrued for a discretionary non-elective contribution for&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">2025</em>&#160;and <ix:nonFraction id="c139161152" contextRef="d_2023-12-03_2024-11-30" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DefinedContributionPlanEmployerDiscretionaryContributionAmount" scale="3" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen" decimals="-3">no</ix:nonFraction> discretionary non-elective contribution for <em style="font: inherit;">2024.</em></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">The defined contribution plan liability recorded in the Consolidated Balance Sheets was<span style="background-color:#ffffff;"> $<ix:nonFraction id="c139161154" contextRef="i_2025-11-29" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:PensionAndOtherPostretirementDefinedBenefitPlansLiabilitiesCurrentAndNoncurrent" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-3">13,011</ix:nonFraction>&#160;</span>and $<ix:nonFraction id="c139161155" contextRef="i_2024-11-30" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:PensionAndOtherPostretirementDefinedBenefitPlansLiabilitiesCurrentAndNoncurrent" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-3">11,992</ix:nonFraction> in&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">2025</em> and <em style="font: inherit;">2024</em>, respectively, for the U.S. Plan and several statutorily required non-U.S. Plans.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b>Defined Benefit Plans</b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">Noncontributory defined benefit pension plans cover all U.S. employees employed prior to <em style="font: inherit;"> January 1, 2007. </em>Benefits for these plans are based primarily on each employee&#8217;s years of service and average compensation. During <em style="font: inherit;">2011,</em> we made significant changes to our U.S. pension plan. The changes included: benefits under the plan were locked-in using service and salary as of <em style="font: inherit;"> May 31, 2011, </em>participants <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> longer earn benefits for future service and salary as they had in the past, affected participants receive a <em style="font: inherit;">three</em> percent increase to the locked-in benefit for every year they continue to work for us and we are making a retirement contribution of <em style="font: inherit;">three</em> percent of eligible compensation to the <em style="font: inherit;">401</em>(k) Plan for those participants.&#160; The funding policy is consistent with the funding requirements of federal law and regulations. Plan assets consist principally of listed equity securities and bonds. Other U.S. postretirement benefits are funded through a Voluntary Employees' Beneficiaries Association Trust.</p>
