   <ix:exclude>&#160;</ix:exclude>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">The discount rate assumption is determined using an actuarial yield curve approach, which results in a discount rate that reflects the characteristics of the plan. The approach identifies a broad population of corporate bonds that meet the quality and size criteria for the particular plan. We use this approach rather than a specific index that has a certain set of bonds that <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>or <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em><em style="font: inherit;">not</em> be representative of the characteristics of our particular plan. A higher discount rate reduces&#160;the present value of the pension obligations. The discount rate for the U.S. pension plan was&#160;<ix:nonFraction id="c139161178" contextRef="i_2025-11-29_RetirementPlanSponsorLocationAxis-US" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:DefinedBenefitPlanAssumptionsUsedCalculatingBenefitObligationDiscountRate" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="4">5.15</ix:nonFraction>&#160;percent at <em style="font: inherit;"> November 29, 2025</em>,&#160;<ix:nonFraction id="c139161179" contextRef="i_2024-11-30_RetirementPlanSponsorLocationAxis-US" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:DefinedBenefitPlanAssumptionsUsedCalculatingBenefitObligationDiscountRate" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="4">5.23</ix:nonFraction> percent at&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> November 30, 2024</em> and&#160;<ix:nonFraction id="c139161180" contextRef="i_2023-12-02_RetirementPlanSponsorLocationAxis-US" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:DefinedBenefitPlanAssumptionsUsedCalculatingBenefitObligationDiscountRate" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="4">5.66</ix:nonFraction> percent at <em style="font: inherit;"> December 2, 2023</em>. Net periodic pension cost for a given fiscal year is based on assumptions developed at the end of the previous fiscal year. A discount rate change of <ix:nonFraction id="c139161181" contextRef="d_2024-12-01_2025-11-29" unitRef="Pure" name="ful:DefinedBenefitPlanAssumptionsUsedCalculatingBenefitObligationIncreaseDecreaseInDiscountRate" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="3">0.5</ix:nonFraction> percentage points at&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> November 29, 2025</em> would impact U.S. pension and other postretirement plan (income) expense by approximately $<ix:nonFraction id="c139161182" contextRef="d_2024-12-01_2025-11-29" unitRef="USD" name="ful:ImpactOnPensionAndOtherPostretirementBenefitExpenseFromAChangeInDiscountRate" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-3">148</ix:nonFraction>&#160;(pre-tax) in fiscal <em style="font: inherit;">2025.</em> Discount rates for non-U.S. plans are determined in a manner consistent with the U.S. plans.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">For the U.S. pension plan, we adopte<span style="background-color:#ffffff;">d the Adjusted Pri-<em style="font: inherit;">2012</em> base mortality table projected generationally using scale MP-<em style="font: inherit;">2021.</em></span></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">The expected long-term rate of return on plan assets assumption for the U.S. pension plan was <ix:nonFraction id="c139161186" contextRef="d_2024-12-01_2025-11-29_RetirementPlanSponsorLocationAxis-US" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:DefinedBenefitPlanAssumptionsUsedCalculatingNetPeriodicBenefitCostExpectedLongTermReturnOnAssets" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="3">7.50</ix:nonFraction>&#160;percent in <em style="font: inherit;">2025</em>&#160;and&#160;<ix:nonFraction id="c139161188" contextRef="d_2023-12-03_2024-11-30_RetirementPlanSponsorLocationAxis-US" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:DefinedBenefitPlanAssumptionsUsedCalculatingNetPeriodicBenefitCostExpectedLongTermReturnOnAssets" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="4">7.75</ix:nonFraction> percent in both&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">2024</em> and&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">2023</em>.&#160;Our expected long-term rate of return on U.S. plan assets was based on our target asset allocation assumption of <ix:nonFraction id="c139161191" contextRef="i_2025-11-29_DefinedBenefitPlanByPlanAssetCategoriesAxis-EquityFundsMember_RetirementPlanSponsorLocationAxis-US" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:DefinedBenefitPlanPlanAssetsTargetAllocationPercentage" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="2">55</ix:nonFraction> percent equities and <ix:nonFraction id="c139161192" contextRef="i_2025-11-29_DefinedBenefitPlanByPlanAssetCategoriesAxis-FixedIncomeFundsMember_RetirementPlanSponsorLocationAxis-US" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:DefinedBenefitPlanPlanAssetsTargetAllocationPercentage" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="2">45</ix:nonFraction> percent fixed-income. Management, in conjunction with our external financial advisors, determines the expected long-term rate of return on plan assets by considering the expected future returns and volatility levels for each asset class that are based on historical returns and forward-looking observations. For <em style="font: inherit;">2025</em>, the expected long-term rate of return on the target equities allocation <span style="background-color:#ffffff;">was <ix:nonFraction id="c139161194" contextRef="d_2024-12-01_2025-11-29_DefinedBenefitPlanByPlanAssetCategoriesAxis-EquityFundsMember_RetirementPlanSponsorLocationAxis-US" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:DefinedBenefitPlanAssumptionsUsedCalculatingNetPeriodicBenefitCostExpectedLongTermReturnOnAssets" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="3">8.50</ix:nonFraction>&#160;p</span>ercent and the expected long-term rate of return on the target fixed-income allocation was <ix:nonFraction id="c139161195" contextRef="d_2024-12-01_2025-11-29_DefinedBenefitPlanByPlanAssetCategoriesAxis-FixedIncomeFundsMember_RetirementPlanSponsorLocationAxis-US" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:DefinedBenefitPlanAssumptionsUsedCalculatingNetPeriodicBenefitCostExpectedLongTermReturnOnAssets" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="3">5.60</ix:nonFraction>&#160;percent. The total plan rate of return assumption included an estimate of the effect of diversification and the plan expense. A change of <ix:nonFraction id="c139161196" contextRef="d_2024-12-01_2025-11-29_RetirementPlanSponsorLocationAxis-US" unitRef="Pure" name="ful:DefinedBenefitPlanAssumptionsUsedCalculatingBenefitObligationIncreaseDecreaseInDiscountRate" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="3">0.5</ix:nonFraction> percentage points for the expected return on assets assumption would impact U.S. net pension and other postretirement plan expense by approxi<span style="background-color:#ffffff;">mately $<ix:nonFraction id="c139161197" contextRef="d_2024-12-01_2025-11-29_RetirementPlanSponsorLocationAxis-US" unitRef="USD" name="ful:ImpactOnPensionAndOtherPostretirementBenefitExpenseFromAChangeInDiscountRate" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-3">2,811</ix:nonFraction>&#160;</span>(pre-tax).</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">Management, in conjunction with our external financial advisors, uses the actual historical rates of return of the asset categories to assess the reasonableness of the expected long-term rate of return on plan assets.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">The expected long-term rate of return on plan assets assumption for non-U.S. pension plans was a weighted-average of&#160;<ix:nonFraction id="c139161198" contextRef="d_2024-12-01_2025-11-29_RetirementPlanSponsorLocationAxis-ForeignPlanMember" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:DefinedBenefitPlanAssumptionsUsedCalculatingNetPeriodicBenefitCostExpectedLongTermReturnOnAssets" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="4">5.03</ix:nonFraction>&#160;percent in&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">2025</em> compared to&#160;<ix:nonFraction id="c139161200" contextRef="d_2023-12-03_2024-11-30_RetirementPlanSponsorLocationAxis-ForeignPlanMember" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:DefinedBenefitPlanAssumptionsUsedCalculatingNetPeriodicBenefitCostExpectedLongTermReturnOnAssets" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="4">5.01</ix:nonFraction> percent in&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">2024</em> and&#160;<ix:nonFraction id="c139161202" contextRef="d_2022-12-04_2023-12-02_RetirementPlanSponsorLocationAxis-ForeignPlanMember" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:DefinedBenefitPlanAssumptionsUsedCalculatingNetPeriodicBenefitCostExpectedLongTermReturnOnAssets" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="4">5.02</ix:nonFraction> percent in <em style="font: inherit;">2023</em>. The expected long-term rate of return on plan assets assumption used in each non-U.S. plan is determined on a plan-by-plan basis for each local jurisdiction and is based on expected future returns for the investment mix of assets currently in the portfolio for that plan.&#160;Management, in conjunction with our external financial advisors, develops expected rates of return for each plan, considers expected long-term returns for each asset category in the plan, reviews expectations for inflation for each local jurisdiction, and estimates the effect of active management of the plan&#8217;s assets. Our largest non-U.S. pension plans are in the United Kingdom and Germany. The expected long-term rate of return on plan assets for the United Kingdom was <ix:nonFraction id="c139161204" contextRef="d_2024-12-01_2025-11-29_RetirementPlanSponsorLocationAxis-GB" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:DefinedBenefitPlanAssumptionsUsedCalculatingNetPeriodicBenefitCostExpectedLongTermReturnOnAssets" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="3">4.50</ix:nonFraction> percent and the expected long-term rate of return on plan assets for Germany was <ix:nonFraction id="c139161205" contextRef="d_2024-12-01_2025-11-29_RetirementPlanSponsorLocationAxis-DE" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:DefinedBenefitPlanAssumptionsUsedCalculatingNetPeriodicBenefitCostExpectedLongTermReturnOnAssets" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="3">5.50</ix:nonFraction>&#160;percent. Management, in conjunction with our external financial advisors, uses actual historical returns of the asset portfolio to assess the reasonableness of the expected rate of return for each plan.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">The projected salary increase assumption is based on historic trends and comparisons to the external market. Higher rates of increase result in higher pension expenses. As this rate is also a long-term expected rate, it is less likely to change on an annual basis.&#160;Under the U.S. pension plan, the compensation amount&#160;was locked-in as of <em style="font: inherit;"> May 31, 2011 </em>and thus the benefit <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> longer includes compensation increases.&#160;</p>

   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><i>Plan Asset Management</i></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">Plan assets are held in trust and invested in mutual funds, separately managed accounts and other commingled investment vehicles holding U.S. and non-U.S. equity securities, fixed income securities and other investment classes. We employ a total return approach whereby a mix of equities and fixed income investments are used to maximize the long-term return of plan assets for a prudent level of risk. Futures and options <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>also be used to enhance risk-adjusted long-term returns while improving portfolio diversification and duration. Risk management is accomplished through diversification across asset classes, utilization of multiple investment managers and general plan-specific investment policies. Risk tolerance is established through careful consideration of the plan liabilities, plan funded status and our assessment of our overall liquidity position. This asset allocation policy mix is reviewed annually and actual versus target allocations are monitored regularly and rebalanced on an as-needed basis. Plan assets are invested using a combination of active and passive investment strategies. Passive, or &#8220;indexed&#8221; strategies, attempt to mimic rather than exceed the investment performance of a market benchmark. The plans&#8217; active investment strategies employ multiple investment management firms which in aggregate cover a range of investment styles and approaches. Performance is monitored and compared to relevant benchmarks on a regular basis.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>

   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">The U.S. pension plans consist of <em style="font: inherit;">two</em> plans: a pension plan and a supplemental executive retirement plan (&#8220;SERP&#8221;). There were <ix:nonFraction id="c139161211" contextRef="i_2025-11-29_RetirementPlanNameAxis-SupplementalExecutiveRetirementPlanMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DefinedBenefitPlanFairValueOfPlanAssets" scale="3" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen" decimals="-3">no</ix:nonFraction> assets in the SERP in&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">2025</em> and <em style="font: inherit;">2024</em>. Consequently, all of the data disclosed in the asset allocation table for the U.S. pension plans pertain to our U.S. pension plan.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">During <em style="font: inherit;">2025</em>, we maintained our assets within the allowed ranges of the target asset alloca<span style="background-color:#ffffff;">tion mix of <ix:nonFraction id="c139161215" contextRef="i_2025-11-29_DefinedBenefitPlanByPlanAssetCategoriesAxis-EquityFundsMember_RetirementPlanNameAxis-SupplementalExecutiveRetirementPlanMember" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:DefinedBenefitPlanPlanAssetsTargetAllocationPercentage" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="2">55</ix:nonFraction> percent equities and <ix:nonFraction id="c139161216" contextRef="i_2025-11-29_DefinedBenefitPlanByPlanAssetCategoriesAxis-FixedIncomeFundsMember_RetirementPlanNameAxis-SupplementalExecutiveRetirementPlanMember" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:DefinedBenefitPlanPlanAssetsTargetAllocationPercentage" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="2">45</ix:nonFraction> pe</span>rcent fixed income plus or minus <em style="font: inherit;">5</em> percent and continued our focus to reduce volatility of plan assets in future periods and to more closely match the duration of the assets with the duration of the liabilities of the plan.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">The non-U.S. pension plans consist of all the pension plans administered outside the U.S., principally consisting of plans in Germany and the United Kingdom. During&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">2025</em>, we maintained our assets for the non-U.S. pension plans at the specific target asset allocation mix determined for each plan plus or minus the allowed rate and continued our focus to reduce volatility of plan assets in future periods and to more closely match the duration of the assets with the duration of the liabilities of the individual plans. We plan to maintain the portfolios at their respective target asset allocations in <em style="font: inherit;">2026.</em></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">Other postretirement benefits plans consist of <em style="font: inherit;">two</em> U.S. plans: a retiree medical health care plan and a group term life insurance plan. There were <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c139161221"><span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c139161489">no</span></span> assets in the group term life insurance plan for&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">2025</em> and <em style="font: inherit;">2024</em>. Consequently, all of the data disclosed in the asset allocation table for other postretirement plans pertain to our retiree medical health care plan. Our investment strategy for other postretirement benefit plans is to own insurance policies that maintain an asset allocation nearly completely in equities. These equities are invested in a passive portfolio indexed to the S&amp;P <em style="font: inherit;">500.</em></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>

   <p style="margin: 0; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt">&#160;</p>
   <p style="margin: 0; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt"><sup style="vertical-align:top;line-height:120%;"><em style="font: inherit;">1</em> </sup>In accordance with ASC Topic <em style="font: inherit;">820</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">10,</em> <i>Fair Value Measurement</i>, certain investments that are measured at NAV (Net Asset Value per share) (or its equivalent) practical expedient have <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> been classified in the fair value hierarchy. The fair value amounts represented in this table are intended to permit reconciliation of the fair value hierarchy to the amounts presented in the statement of financial position.</p>
   <p style="margin: 0; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt">&#160;</p>
   <p style="margin: 0; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt">The definitions of fair values of our pension and other postretirement benefit plan assets at&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> November 29, 2025 </em>and <em style="font: inherit;"> November 30, 2024</em> by asset category are as follows:</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="background-color:#FFFFFF;font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b><i>Equities</i></b>&#8212;Primarily publicly traded common stock for purposes of total return and to maintain equity exposure consistent with policy allocations. Investments include: (i) U.S. and non-U.S. equity securities and mutual funds valued at closing prices from national exchanges; and (ii) commingled funds valued at unit values or net asset values provided by the investment managers, which are based on the fair value of the underlying investments. Funds valued at net asset value have various investment strategies including seeking maximum total returns consistent with prudent investment management, seeking current income consistent with preservation of capital and daily liquidity and seeking to approximate the risk and return characterized by a specific index fund. There are <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> restrictions for redeeming holdings out of these funds and the funds have <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> unfunded commitments.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b><i>Fixed income</i></b>&#8212;Primarily corporate and government debt securities for purposes of total return and managing fixed income exposure to policy allocations. Investments include (i) mutual funds valued at closing prices from national exchanges, (ii) corporate and government debt securities valued at closing prices from national exchanges, (iii) commingled funds valued at unit values or net asset value provided by the investment managers, which are based on the fair value of the underlying investments, and (iv) an annuity contract, the value of which is determined by the provider and represents the amount the plan would receive if the contract were cashed out at year-end.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b><i>Insurance</i></b>&#8212;Insurance contracts for purposes of funding postretirement medical benefits. Fair values are the cash surrender values as determined by the providers which are the amounts the plans would receive if the contracts were cashed out at year end.</p>
   <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b><i>Cash</i></b><i>&#8211;</i>Cash balances on hand, accrued income and pending settlements of transactions for purposes of handling plan payments. Fair values are the cash balances as reported by the Trustees of the plans.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>

   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">The difference between the change in the deferred tax liability on the balance sheet and the deferred tax provision is primarily related to the defined benefit pension plan adjustment and hedges recorded in accumulated other comprehensive income (loss) offset by liabilities established in purchase accounting.</p>

   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">Valuation allowances primarily relate&#160;to foreign net operating loss carryforwards and branch foreign tax credit carryforwards where the future potential benefits do <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> meet the more-likely-than-<em style="font: inherit;">not</em> realization test. The decrease in the valuation allowance is primarily related to a decrease in foreign net operating losses for which the Company does <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> expect to receive a full tax benefit.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">Deferred tax assets and liabilities are measured using the currently enacted tax rates that apply to taxable income in effect for the years in which those deferred tax assets and liabilities are expected to be realized or settled. We record a valuation allowance to reduce deferred tax assets to the amount that is believed more-likely-than-<em style="font: inherit;">not</em> to be realized. We believe it is more-likely-than-<em style="font: inherit;">not</em> that&#160;reversal of deferred tax liabilities and forecasted income&#160;will be sufficient to fully recover the net deferred tax assets <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> already offset by a valuation allowance. In the event that all or part of the gross deferred tax assets are determined <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> to be realizable in the future, an adjustment to the valuation allowance would be charged to earnings in the period such determination is made.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">U.S. income taxes have <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> been provided on approximately $<ix:nonFraction id="c139161248" contextRef="d_2024-12-01_2025-11-29" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:UndistributedEarnings" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-3">1,365,208</ix:nonFraction> of undistributed earnings of non-U.S. subsidiaries. We intend to indefinitely reinvest these undistributed earnings. Cash available in the United States has historically been sufficient and we expect it will continue to be sufficient to fund U.S. cash flow requirements. In the event these earnings are later distributed to the U.S., such distributions would likely result in additional U.S. tax.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">While non-U.S. operations have been profitable overall, there are cumulative tax losses of $<ix:nonFraction id="c139161249" contextRef="i_2025-11-29_IncomeTaxAuthorityAxis-ForeignCountryMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:OperatingLossCarryforwards" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-3">69,673</ix:nonFraction>&#160;in various countries. These tax losses can be carried forward to offset the income tax liabilities on future income in these countries. Cumulative tax losses of $<ix:nonFraction id="c139161250" contextRef="i_2025-11-29_IncomeTaxAuthorityAxis-ForeignCountryMember_TaxPeriodAxis-IndefiniteMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:OperatingLossCarryforwards" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-3">46,198</ix:nonFraction>&#160;can be carried forward indefinitely, while the remaining $<ix:nonFraction id="c139161251" contextRef="i_2025-11-29_IncomeTaxAuthorityAxis-ForeignCountryMember_TaxPeriodAxis-TaxPeriod2026To2043Member" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:OperatingLossCarryforwards" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-3">23,475</ix:nonFraction> of tax losses must be utilized during <em style="font: inherit;">2026</em> to <em style="font: inherit;">2043.</em></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">The U.S. has a branch foreign tax credit carryforward of $<ix:nonFraction id="c139161254" contextRef="i_2025-11-29_TaxCreditCarryforwardAxis-BranchForeignTaxCreditCarryforwardMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:TaxCreditCarryforwardAmount" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-3">4,337</ix:nonFraction>. A valuation allowance has been recorded against this foreign tax credit carryforward to reflect that this amount is <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> more-likely-than-<em style="font: inherit;">not</em> to be realized.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>

   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b>Note <em style="font: inherit;">12:</em> Financial Instruments</b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b>&#160;</b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i>Overview</i></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">As a result of being a global enterprise, foreign currency exchange rates and fluctuations in those rates <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>affect the Company's net investment in foreign subsidiaries and our earnings, cash flows and financial position are exposed to foreign currency risk from foreign currency denominated receivables and payables.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">We use foreign currency forward contracts, cross-currency swaps,&#160;interest rate swaps and net investment hedges to manage risks associated with foreign currency exchange rates and interest rates. We do <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> hold derivative financial instruments of a speculative nature or for trading purposes. We record derivatives as assets and liabilities on the balance sheet at fair value. Changes in fair value are recognized immediately in earnings unless the derivative qualifies and is designated as a hedge. Cash flows from derivatives are classified in the Consolidated Statement of Cash Flows in the same category as the cash flows from the items subject to designated hedge or undesignated (economic) hedge relationships. We evaluate&#160;hedge effectiveness at inception and on an ongoing basis. If a derivative is <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> longer expected to be effective, hedge accounting is discontinued. Hedge ineffectiveness, if any, is recorded in earnings.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">We are exposed to credit risk in the event of nonperformance of counterparties for foreign currency forward exchange contracts and interest rate swap agreements. We select investment-grade multinational banks and financial institutions as counterparties for derivative transactions and monitor the credit quality of each of these banks on a periodic basis as warranted. We do <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> anticipate nonperformance by any of these counterparties, and valuation allowances, if any, are <i>de minimis</i>.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>

   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i><span style="background-color:#ffffff;">Cash Flow Hedges</span></i></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">On <em style="font: inherit;"> January 12, 2023, </em>we entered into an interest rate swap agreement to convert $<ix:nonFraction id="c139161281" contextRef="i_2023-01-13_DerivativeInstrumentRiskAxis-InterestRateSwap3Member" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DerivativeAmountOfHedgedItem" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-8">400,000</ix:nonFraction> of our variable rate <em style="font: inherit;">1</em>-month LIBOR debt to a fixed rate of&#160;<ix:nonFraction id="c139161283" contextRef="i_2023-01-13_DerivativeInstrumentRiskAxis-InterestRateSwap3Member" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:DerivativeFixedInterestRate" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="6">3.6895</ix:nonFraction> percent that matures on <em style="font: inherit;"> January 12, 2028. </em>On <em style="font: inherit;"> February 28, 2023, </em>after refinancing our debt, we amended the interest rate swap agreement to our <em style="font: inherit;">1</em>-month SOFR debt to a fixed rate of <ix:nonFraction id="c139161285" contextRef="i_2023-02-28_DerivativeInstrumentRiskAxis-InterestRateSwap3Member" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:DerivativeFixedInterestRate" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="5">3.7260</ix:nonFraction> in accordance with the practical expedients included in ASC <em style="font: inherit;">848,</em> <i>Reference Rate Reform</i>. The combined fair&#160;value of the interest rate swap w<span style="background-color:#ffffff;">as a&#160;liability of $<ix:nonFraction id="c139161287" contextRef="i_2025-11-29_DerivativeInstrumentRiskAxis-InterestRateSwap3Member" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:InterestRateCashFlowHedgeLiabilityAtFairValue" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-3">3,944</ix:nonFraction> at </span><em style="font: inherit;"> November 29, 2025</em><span style="background-color:#ffffff;"> and was included in other liabilities&#160;in the</span> Consolidated Balance Sheets. The&#160;swap was designated for hedge accounting treatment as a cash flow hedge. We are applying the hypothetical derivative method to assess hedge effectiveness&#160;for this interest rate swap. Changes in the fair value of a hypothetically perfect swap with terms that match the critical terms of our variable rate debt are&#160;compared with the change in the fair value of the swap.</p>
   <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><span style="background-color:#ffffff;">On <em style="font: inherit;"> March 16, 2023, </em>we entered into an interest rate swap agreement to convert $<ix:nonFraction id="c139161288" contextRef="i_2023-03-16_DerivativeInstrumentRiskAxis-InterestRateSwapMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DerivativeAmountOfHedgedItem" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-8">300,000</ix:nonFraction> of our <em style="font: inherit;">1</em>-month SOFR debt to a fixed rate of <ix:nonFraction id="c139161290" contextRef="i_2023-03-16_DerivativeInstrumentRiskAxis-InterestRateSwapMember" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:DerivativeFixedInterestRate" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="5">3.7210</ix:nonFraction> percent that&#160;matures on <em style="font: inherit;"> February 15, 2028. </em>The combined fair value of the interest rate swap was a&#160;liability of $<ix:nonFraction id="c139161291" contextRef="i_2025-11-29_DerivativeInstrumentRiskAxis-InterestRateSwapMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:InterestRateCashFlowHedgeLiabilityAtFairValue" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-3">3,143</ix:nonFraction>&#160;at </span><em style="font: inherit;"> November 29, 2025</em><span style="background-color:#ffffff;"> and was included in other&#160;liabilities in the Consolidated Balance Sheets. The swap was designated for hedge accounting treatment as a cash flow hedge. We are applying the hypothetical&#160;derivative method to assess h</span>edge effectiveness for this interest rate swap. Changes in the fair value of a hypothetically perfect swap with terms that match the&#160;critical terms of our variable rate debt are compared with the change in the fair value of the swaps.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">On <em style="font: inherit;"> March 16, 2023, </em>we entered into an interest rate swap agreement to convert $<ix:nonFraction id="c139161292" contextRef="i_2023-03-16_DerivativeInstrumentRiskAxis-InterestRateSwap2Member" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DerivativeAmountOfHedgedItem" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-8">100,000</ix:nonFraction> of our <em style="font: inherit;">1</em>-month SOFR debt to a fixed rate of <ix:nonFraction id="c139161294" contextRef="i_2023-03-16_DerivativeInstrumentRiskAxis-InterestRateSwap2Member" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:DerivativeFixedInterestRate" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="5">3.8990</ix:nonFraction> percent that&#160;matures on <em style="font: inherit;"> February 15, 2028. </em>The combined fair value of the interest rate swap was <span style="background-color:#ffffff;">a&#160;liability&#160;of $<ix:nonFraction id="c139161295" contextRef="i_2025-11-29_DerivativeInstrumentRiskAxis-InterestRateSwap2Member" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:InterestRateCashFlowHedgeLiabilityAtFairValue" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-3">1,411</ix:nonFraction>&#160;at</span> <em style="font: inherit;"> November 29, 2025</em><span style="background-color:#ffffff;"> and was included in other&#160;liabilities in the</span> Consolidated Balance Sheets. The swap was designated for hedge accounting treatment as a cash flow hedge. We are applying the hypothetical&#160;derivative method to assess hedge effectiveness for these interest rate swaps. Changes in the fair value of a hypothetically perfect swap with terms that match&#160;the critical terms of our variable rate debt are compared with the change in the fair value of the swaps.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left"><span style="color:#000000;"><i><span style="background-color:#ffffff">Net Investment Hedges</span></i></span></p>
   <p style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; margin: 0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><span style="color:#000000;">On <em style="font: inherit;"> October 17, 2022, </em>we entered into a float-to-float cross-currency interest rate swap agreement with a notional amount of <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c139161296">&#8364;307,173</span> maturing in <em style="font: inherit;"> October 2028. </em>On <em style="font: inherit;"> October 20, 2022, </em>we entered into fixed-to-fixed cross-currency interest rate swap agreements for a total notional amount of <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c139161297">&#8364;300,000</span> with tranches maturing in <em style="font: inherit;"> August 2025, </em><em style="font: inherit;"> August 2026 </em>and <em style="font: inherit;"> February 2027.&#160;</em></span>On <em style="font: inherit;"> July 18, 2025, </em>we amended the agreement for the <em style="font: inherit;">two</em> tranches of the fixed-to-fixed cross-currency interest rate swap, of <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c139161299">&#8364;50,000</span> each, that matured in <em style="font: inherit;"> August 2025 </em>to a maturity date of <em style="font: inherit;"> February 2027.&#160;</em><span style="color:#000000;">On <em style="font: inherit;"> June 30, 2023, </em><em style="font: inherit;">1</em>-month LIBOR rates ceased to exist and the IBOR Fallbacks Protocol published&#160;by the International Swaps and Derivatives Association (ISDA) took effect as outlined in the interest rate swap agreement. As a result, the <em style="font: inherit;">1</em>-month LIBOR leg&#160;of the float-to-float agreement was converted to Overnight SOFR plus <ix:nonFraction id="c139161302" contextRef="i_2023-06-30_DerivativeInstrumentRiskAxis-CrossCurrencyInterestRateContractMember_VariableRateAxis-SecuredOvernightFinancingRateSofrOvernightIndexSwapRateMember" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:DerivativeVariableInterestRate" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="4">3.28</ix:nonFraction> percent. On <em style="font: inherit;"> July 17, 2023, </em>we amended the <em style="font: inherit;">1</em>-month EURIBOR leg of the float-to-float&#160;agreement to Overnight ESTR plus <ix:nonFraction id="c139161304" contextRef="i_2023-07-17_DerivativeInstrumentRiskAxis-CrossCurrencyInterestRateContractMember_VariableRateAxis-EuroShortTermRateESTROvernightIndexSwapRateMember" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:DerivativeVariableInterestRate" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="6">3.2195</ix:nonFraction> percent. We applied the practical expedients included in ASC <em style="font: inherit;">848,</em> <i>Reference Rate Reform</i>.&#160;As of </span><em style="font: inherit;"> November 29, 2025</em><span style="color:#000000;">, the combined fair value of the swaps wa<span style="background-color:#ffffff;">s a liability of $<ix:nonFraction id="c139161306" contextRef="i_2025-11-29_DerivativeInstrumentRiskAxis-CrossCurrencyInterestRateContractMember_VariableRateAxis-EuroShortTermRateESTROvernightIndexSwapRateMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:InterestRateFairValueHedgeLiabilityAtFairValue" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-3">113,144</ix:nonFraction> and was included in other liabilities in the Consolidated Balance Sheets. The cross-currency interest rate swaps hedge a portion of the Company&#8217;s investment in Euro denominated foreign subsidiaries.</span></span></p>
   <p style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><span style="color:#000000;">The swaps are designated as net investment hedges for accounting treatment. The net gains or losses attributable to changes in spot exchange rates are recorded in the cumulative translation adjustment within other comprehensi<span style="background-color:#ffffff;">ve income (loss). T</span>he gains or losses are reclassified into earnings upon a liquidation event or deconsolidation of the foreign subsidiary. Any ineffective portions of net investment hedges are reclassified from accumulated other comprehensive (loss)&#160;<span style="background-color:#ffffff;">income&#160;int</span>o earnings during the period of change. The amount in accumulated other comprehensive <span style="background-color:#ffffff;">(loss)&#160;income&#160;relate</span>d to net investment hedge cross-currency sw<span style="background-color:#ffffff;">aps was a loss of </span>$<ix:nonFraction id="c139161307" contextRef="d_2024-12-01_2025-11-29_DerivativeInstrumentRiskAxis-CrossCurrencyInterestRateContractMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:OtherComprehensiveIncomeLossCashFlowHedgeGainLossBeforeReclassificationAndTax" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-4" sign="-">85,610</ix:nonFraction><span style="background-color:#ffffff;">&#160;as</span> of </span><em style="font: inherit;"> November 29, 2025</em><span style="color:#000000;">.&#160;As of </span><em style="font: inherit;"> November 29, 2025</em><span style="color:#000000;">,&#160;</span>we reclassif<span style="background-color:#ffffff;">ied $<ix:nonFraction id="c139161308" contextRef="d_2024-12-01_2025-11-29_DerivativeInstrumentRiskAxis-CrossCurrencyInterestRateContractMember_DerivativeInstrumentsGainLossByHedgingRelationshipAxis-NetInvestmentHedgingMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:ForeignCurrencyCashFlowHedgeGainLossReclassifiedToEarningsNet" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-3">261</ix:nonFraction> of losses into earnings from net investment hedges and we expect to reclassify $<ix:nonFraction id="c139161309" contextRef="i_2025-11-29_DerivativeInstrumentRiskAxis-CrossCurrencyInterestRateContractMember_DerivativeInstrumentsGainLossByHedgingRelationshipAxis-NetInvestmentHedgingMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:ForeignCurrencyCashFlowHedgeGainLossToBeReclassifiedDuringNext12Months" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-4" sign="-">350</ix:nonFraction>&#160;of losses into earnings within the next <em style="font: inherit;">twelve</em> months. This is related to the portion excluded from the assessment of hedge effectiveness for the net investment hedges in the amount of $<ix:nonFraction id="c139161311" contextRef="d_2024-12-01_2025-11-29_DerivativeInstrumentRiskAxis-CrossCurrencyInterestRateContractMember_DerivativeInstrumentsGainLossByHedgingRelationshipAxis-NetInvestmentHedgingMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:GainLossFromComponentsExcludedFromAssessmentOfCashFlowHedgeEffectivenessNet" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">700</ix:nonFraction>.&#160;</span></p>

   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i><span style="background-color:#ffffff;">Fair Value Hedges</span></i></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><span style="background-color:#ffffff;">On <em style="font: inherit;"> February 12, 2021, </em>we entered into&#160;interest rate swap agreements to convert our $<ix:nonFraction id="c139161312" contextRef="i_2021-02-12_DerivativeInstrumentRiskAxis-InterestRateSwapRelatedToPublicNotesMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DerivativeAmountOfHedgedItem" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-8">300,000</ix:nonFraction>&#160;Public Notes that were issued on <em style="font: inherit;"> October&#160;</em><em style="font: inherit;">20,</em> <em style="font: inherit;">2020</em> to a variable interest rate of <em style="font: inherit;">1</em>-month LIBOR plus <ix:nonFraction id="c139161316" contextRef="i_2021-02-12_DerivativeInstrumentRiskAxis-InterestRateSwapRelatedToPublicNotesMember_VariableRateAxis-LondonInterbankOfferedRateLibor1Member" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:DerivativeVariableInterestRate" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="4">3.28</ix:nonFraction> percent. On <em style="font: inherit;"> June 30, 2023, </em><em style="font: inherit;">1</em>-month LIBOR rates ceased to exist and the IBOR Fallbacks Protocol published by the&#160;International Swaps and Derivatives Association ("ISDA") took effect as outlined in the interest rate swap agreement. As </span>a result, the interest rate swap&#160;agreement&#160;was&#160;converted to Overnight SOFR plus <ix:nonFraction id="c139161318" contextRef="i_2021-02-12_DerivativeInstrumentRiskAxis-InterestRateSwapRelatedToPublicNotesMember_VariableRateAxis-LondonInterbankOfferedRateLibor1Member" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:DerivativeVariableInterestRate" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="4">3.28</ix:nonFraction> percent. We applied the practical expedients included in ASC <em style="font: inherit;">848,</em> <i>Reference Rate Reform</i>.&#160;See Note <em style="font: inherit;">7</em> for further discussion on the issuance of our Public Notes. These interest rate swap agreements mature on <em style="font: inherit;"> October 15, 2028. </em>The combined fair value of the interest rate swap<span style="background-color:#ffffff;">s&#160;was a liability of $<ix:nonFraction id="c139161321" contextRef="i_2025-11-29_BalanceSheetLocationAxis-OtherLiabilitiesMember_DerivativeInstrumentRiskAxis-InterestRateSwapRelatedToPublicNotesMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:InterestRateFairValueHedgeLiabilityAtFairValue" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-3">20,481</ix:nonFraction>&#160;at </span><em style="font: inherit;"> November 29, 2025</em><span style="background-color:#ffffff;">, and was included in other liabilities in the Cons</span>olidated Balance Sheets.&#160;The swaps were&#160;designated for hedge accounting treatment as fair value hedges. We apply the short cut method and assume hedge effectiveness. Changes in the fair value of a hypothetically perfect swap with terms that match the critical terms of our $<ix:nonFraction id="c139161322" contextRef="i_2025-11-29_LongtermDebtTypeAxis-PublicNotesMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentFaceAmount" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-8">300,000</ix:nonFraction> fixed rate Public Notes are compared with the change in the fair value of the swaps.&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i>Derivatives <em style="font: inherit;">Not</em> Designated As Hedging Instruments</i></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">The Company uses foreign currency forward contracts to offset its exposure to the change in value of certain foreign currency denominated assets and liabilities held at foreign subsidiaries that are remeasured at the end of each period. Although the contracts are effective economic hedges, they are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> designated as accounting hedges. Foreign currency forward contracts are recorded as assets and liabilities on the balance sheet at fair value. Changes in the value of these derivatives are recognized immediately in earnings, thereby offsetting the current earnings effect of the related foreign currency denominated assets and liabilities. See Note <em style="font: inherit;">13</em> for fair value amounts of these derivative instruments.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">As of <em style="font: inherit;"> November 29, 2025</em>, we had forward foreign currency contracts maturing<span style="background-color:#ffffff;"> between <em style="font: inherit;"> December 1, 2025&#160;</em>and <em style="font: inherit;"> February 4, 2026. </em>The mark-to-market effect associated with these contracts was largely offset by the underlying transaction gains and </span>losses resulting from the foreign currency exposures for which these contracts relate.</p>

   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">The amounts of<span style="background-color:#ffffff;"> pretax gains&#160;(losses</span>) recogn<span style="background-color:#ffffff;">ized in other (expense) income, net related to d</span>erivative instruments <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> designated as hedging instruments are as follows:</p>

   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">Concentrations of credit risk with respect to trade accounts receivable are limited due to the large number of entities in the customer base and their dispersion across many different industries and countries. As of <em style="font: inherit;"> November 29, 2025</em>, there were <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> significant concentrations of credit risk.</p>

  <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2024-12-01_2025-11-29" name="us-gaap:FairValueDisclosuresTextBlock" id="c3087023" escape="true">
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b>Note <em style="font: inherit;">13:</em> Fair Value Measurements&#160;</b></p>
   <p style="background-color:#FFFFFF;font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b><i>&#160;</i></b></p>
   <p style="background-color:#FFFFFF;font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i>Overview</i></p>
   <p style="background-color:#FFFFFF;font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="background-color:#FFFFFF;font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">Estimates of fair value for financial assets and liabilities are based on the framework established in the accounting guidance for fair value measurements. The framework defines fair value, provides guidance for measuring fair value and requires certain disclosures. The framework discusses valuation techniques, such as the market approach (comparable market prices), the income approach (present value of future income or cash flow) and the cost approach (cost to replace the service capacity of an asset or replacement cost). The framework utilizes a fair value hierarchy that prioritizes the inputs to valuation techniques used to measure fair value into <em style="font: inherit;">three</em> broad levels. The following is a brief description of those <em style="font: inherit;">three</em> levels:</p>
   <p style="background-color:#FFFFFF;font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
   <table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="width:100%;font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;"><tbody><tr><td style="width:18pt;">&#160;</td><td style="width:18pt;vertical-align:top;"> <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; background-color: rgb(255, 255, 255); font-size: 10pt;">&#9679;</p> </td><td style="vertical-align:top;"> <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; background-color: rgb(255, 255, 255); font-size: 10pt;">Level <em style="font: inherit;">1:</em> Observable inputs such as quoted prices (unadjusted) in active markets for identical assets or liabilities.</p> </td></tr>
</tbody></table>
   <table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="width:100%;font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;"><tbody><tr><td style="width:18pt;">&#160;</td><td style="width:18pt;vertical-align:top;"> <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; background-color: rgb(255, 255, 255); font-size: 10pt;">&#9679;</p> </td><td style="vertical-align:top;"> <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; background-color: rgb(255, 255, 255); font-size: 10pt;">Level <em style="font: inherit;">2:</em> Inputs other than quoted prices that are observable for the asset or liability, either directly or indirectly. These include quoted prices for similar assets or liabilities in active markets and quoted prices for identical or similar assets or liabilities in markets that are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> active.</p> </td></tr>
</tbody></table>
   <table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="width:100%;font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;"><tbody><tr><td style="width:18pt;">&#160;</td><td style="width:18pt;vertical-align:top;"> <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; background-color: rgb(255, 255, 255); font-size: 10pt;">&#9679;</p> </td><td style="vertical-align:top;"> <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; background-color: rgb(255, 255, 255); font-size: 10pt;">Level <em style="font: inherit;">3:</em> Unobservable inputs that reflect management&#8217;s assumptions, and include situations where there is little, if any, market activity for the asset or liability.</p> </td></tr>
</tbody></table>
   <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i>Balances Measured at Fair Value on a Recurring Basis</i></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">The following table presents information about our financial assets and liabilities that are measured at fair value on a recurring basis as of <em style="font: inherit;"> November 29, 2025 </em>and <em style="font: inherit;"> November 30, 2024</em>, and indicates the fair value hierarchy of the valuation techniques utilized to determine such fair value.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;">&#160;</p>

   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><i>Balances Measured at Fair Value on a Nonrecurring Basis</i></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">We measure certain assets and liabilities at fair value on a nonrecurring basis. These assets include&#160;intangible assets acquired&#160;in an acquisition. The identified intangible assets of customer relationships, technology and tradenames acquired in connection with our acquisitions were measured using unobservable (Level&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">3</em>) inputs. The fair value of the intangible assets was calculated using either the income or cost approach. Significant inputs include estimated revenue growth rates, gross margins, operating expenses, attrition rate, royalty rate and discount rate.&#160;&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt;">See Note&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">2</em>&#160;for further discussion regarding our acquisitions.</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt;">See Note <em style="font: inherit;">7</em> for discussion regarding the fair value of debt.</p>

   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b>Note <em style="font: inherit;">14:</em> Commitments and Contingencies</b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i>&#160;</i></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i>Environmental Matters</i><i>&#160;</i></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">From time to time, we become aware of compliance matters relating to, or receive notices from, federal, state or local entities regarding possible or alleged violations of environmental, health or safety laws and regulations. We review the circumstances of each individual site, considering the number of parties involved, the level of potential liability or our contribution relative to the other parties, the nature and magnitude of the hazardous substances involved, the method and extent of remediation, the estimated legal and consulting expense with respect to each site and the time period over which any costs would likely be incurred. Also, from time to time, we are identified as a potentially responsible party (&#8220;PRP&#8221;) under the Comprehensive Environmental Response, Compensation and Liability Act ("CERCLA") and/or similar state laws that impose liability for costs relating to the clean up of contamination resulting from past spills, disposal or other release of hazardous substances. We are also subject to similar laws in some of the countries where current and former facilities are located. Our environmental, health and safety department monitors compliance with applicable laws on a global basis. To the extent we can reasonably estimate the amount of our probable liabilities for environmental matters, we establish an undiscounted financial provision.&#160;We recorded <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c139161505"><span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c139161506">liabilities</span></span> of $<ix:nonFraction id="c139161344" contextRef="i_2025-11-29" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:AccrualForEnvironmentalLossContingencies" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-3">2,625</ix:nonFraction>&#160;and $<ix:nonFraction id="c139161345" contextRef="i_2024-11-30" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:AccrualForEnvironmentalLossContingencies" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-3">3,445</ix:nonFraction>&#160;as of <em style="font: inherit;"> November 29, 2025 </em>and <em style="font: inherit;"> November 30, 2024</em>, respectively, for probable and reasonably estimable environmental remediation costs.&#160;Of the amount reserved, $<ix:nonFraction id="c139161346" contextRef="i_2025-11-29_EnvironmentalRemediationSiteAxis-FacilityInSimpsonvilleSouthCarolinaMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:AccrualForEnvironmentalLossContingencies" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-3">277</ix:nonFraction>&#160;and $<ix:nonFraction id="c139161347" contextRef="i_2024-11-30_EnvironmentalRemediationSiteAxis-FacilityInSimpsonvilleSouthCarolinaMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:AccrualForEnvironmentalLossContingencies" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-3">1,055</ix:nonFraction>&#160;as of <em style="font: inherit;"> November 29, 2025 </em>and <em style="font: inherit;"> November 30, 2024</em>, respectively, is attributable to a facility we own in Simpsonville, South Carolina as a result of our Royal Adhesives acquisition that is a designated site under CERCLA.</p>
   <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">Currently we are involved in various environmental investigations, clean up activities and administrative proceedings and lawsuits. In particular, we are currently deemed a PRP in conjunction with numerous other parties, in a number of government enforcement actions associated with landfills and/or hazardous waste sites. As a PRP, we <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>be required to pay a share of the costs of investigation and clean up of these sites. In addition, we are engaged in environmental remediation and monitoring efforts at a number of current and former operating facilities. While uncertainties exist with respect to the amounts and timing of the ultimate environmental liabilities, based on currently available information, we have concluded that these matters, individually or in the aggregate, will <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> have a material adverse effect on our results of operations, financial condition or cash flow.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i>Other Legal Proceedings</i><i>&#160;</i></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">From time to time and in the ordinary course of business, we are a party to, or a target of, lawsuits, claims, investigations and proceedings, including product liability, personal injury, contract, patent and intellectual property, environmental, health and safety, tax and employment matters. While we are unable to predict the outcome of these matters, we have concluded, based upon currently available information, that the ultimate resolution of any pending matter, individually or in the aggregate, including the asbestos litigation described in the following paragraphs, will <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> have a material adverse effect on our results of operations, financial condition or cash flow.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">We have been named as a defendant in lawsuits in which plaintiffs have alleged injury due to products containing asbestos manufactured more than <em style="font: inherit;">35</em> years ago. The plaintiffs generally bring these lawsuits against multiple defendants and seek damages (both actual and punitive) in very large amounts. In many cases, plaintiffs are unable to demonstrate that they have suffered any compensable injuries or that the injuries suffered were the result of exposure to products manufactured by us. We are typically dismissed as a defendant in such cases without payment. If the plaintiff presents evidence indicating that compensable injury occurred as a result of exposure to our products, the case is generally settled for an amount that reflects the seriousness of the injury, the length, intensity and character of exposure to products containing asbestos, the number and solvency of other defendants in the case, and the jurisdiction in which the case has been brought.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">A significant portion of the defense costs and settlements in asbestos-related litigation is paid by <em style="font: inherit;">third</em> parties, including indemnification pursuant to the provisions of a <em style="font: inherit;">1976</em> agreement under which we acquired a business from a <em style="font: inherit;">third</em> party. Currently, this <em style="font: inherit;">third</em> party is defending and paying settlement amounts, under a reservation of rights, in most of the asbestos cases tendered to the <em style="font: inherit;">third</em> party.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">In addition to the indemnification arrangements with <em style="font: inherit;">third</em> parties, we have insurance policies that generally provide coverage for asbestos liabilities, including defense costs. Historically, insurers have paid a significant portion of our defense costs and settlements in asbestos-related litigation. However, certain of our insurers are insolvent.&#160; We have entered into cost-sharing agreements with our insurers that provide for the allocation of defense costs and settlements and judgments in asbestos-related lawsuits. These agreements require, among other things, that we fund a share of settlements and judgments allocable to years in which the responsible insurer is insolvent.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">A summary of the number of and settlement amounts for asbestos-related lawsuits and claims is as follows:</p>

   <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">We do <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> believe that it would be meaningful to disclose the aggregate number of asbestos-related lawsuits filed against us because relatively few of these lawsuits are known to involve exposure to asbestos-containing products that we manufactured. Rather, we believe it is more meaningful to disclose the number of lawsuits that are settled and result in a payment to the plaintiff. To the extent we can reasonably estimate the amount of our probable liabilities for pending asbestos-related claims, we establish a financial provision and a corresponding receivable for insurance recoveries.&#160;</p>

   <ix:exclude>&#160;</ix:exclude>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">In&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> February 2024,&#160;</em>the named plaintiffs in&#160;<i>Rouse et al. v. H.B. Fuller Company et al.</i>&#160;filed a&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">third</em>&#160;amended complaint in their lawsuit against the Company and&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">one</em>&#160;of its subsidiaries, which was initiated in&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> September 2022.&#160;</em>The suit is pending in the federal District of Minnesota and seeks damages arising from property damage attributed to alleged defects in grout sold by the Company&#8217;s divested North America Flooring business. As previously disclosed, the court ordered the parties and their insurers to attend a meditation session on <em style="font: inherit;"> October 21&#160;</em>and&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">22,</em>&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">2025</em><i>.</i>&#160;At that mediation session, the Company and the plaintiffs agreed in principle to settle this matter for up to $<ix:nonFraction id="c139161363" contextRef="d_2024-02-01_2024-02-28_LitigationCaseAxis-RouseEtAlVHbFullerMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:LitigationSettlementAmountAwardedToOtherParty" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-6">75.0</ix:nonFraction> million. Under the proposed settlement, in lieu of funding the maximum settlement amount, the Company&#8217;s payment obligations will be limited to validly submitted claims, settlement administration costs, service awards, and plaintiffs&#8217; attorneys&#8217; fees and expenses.<b> </b>The terms of a definitive settlement agreement are being negotiated and will be subject to court approval. In light of these developments, the Company concluded that a loss is probable and reasonably estimable and recorded an accrual in anticipation of the settlement of $<ix:nonFraction id="c139161364" contextRef="d_2024-02-01_2024-02-28_LitigationCaseAxis-RouseEtAlVHbFullerMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:LitigationSettlementLoss" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">34.8</ix:nonFraction> million ($<ix:nonFraction id="c139161365" contextRef="d_2024-02-01_2024-02-28_LitigationCaseAxis-RouseEtAlVHbFullerMember" unitRef="USD" name="ful:LitigationSettlementLossAfterTax" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">26.3</ix:nonFraction> million after tax) based on a range of possible outcomes. This accrual is included in other accrued expenses in the Consolidated Balance Sheets as of <em style="font: inherit;"> November 29, 2025. </em>The Company believes that it is entitled to reimbursement from its insurers for a substantial portion of the potential settlement amount as well as legal fees already incurred and paid and is actively pursuing reimbursement from its insurers.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">Based on currently available information, we have concluded that the resolution of any pending matter, including asbestos-related litigation, individually or in the aggregate, will <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> have a material adverse effect on our results of operations, financial condition or cash flow.</p>
   <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&#160;</p>

  <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2024-12-01_2025-11-29" name="us-gaap:SegmentReportingDisclosureTextBlock" id="c3087029" escape="true">
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:13.7pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;text-indent:-13.7pt;"><b>Note <em style="font: inherit;">15:</em> Segments</b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">We are required to report segment information in the same way that we internally organize our business for assessing performance and making decisions regarding allocation of resources.&#160;Revenue and Adjusted EBITDA of each of our segments are regularly reviewed by our chief executive officer, who acts as our chief operating decision maker, to make decisions about resources to be allocated to the segments and assess their performance. Adjusted EBITDA is defined as net income before interest, income taxes, depreciation and amortization&#160;and foreign currency gain/loss, adjusted for other items within a relevant period which are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> reflective of the segment&#8217;s operating performance in the period.&#160;Corporate expenses, other than those included in Corporate Unallocated, are allocated to each operating segment.&#160;Consistent with our internal management reporting, Corporate Unallocated includes and Adjusted EBITDA excludes amounts related to business acquisition and integration costs, organizational restructuring charges and project costs associated with our implementation of Project ONE. Corporate assets are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> allocated to the operating segments. Inter-segment revenues are recorded at cost plus a markup for administrative costs.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">As of <em style="font: inherit;"> November 30, 2024, </em>our <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c139161370">three</span> operating segments consisted of Hygiene, Health and Consumable Adhesives, Engineering Adhesives and Construction Adhesives.&#160;As of the beginning of fiscal <em style="font: inherit;">2025,</em> we reorganized our operating segments&#160;by selling our North America Flooring business, previously part of the Construction Adhesives operating segment, and combining our Insulated Glass, Woodworking&#160;and Composite businesses, previously part of the Engineering Adhesives operating segment, with Construction Adhesives Roofing and Building Envelope and Infrastructure businesses to form the Building Adhesive Solutions operating segment. All financial results related to North America Flooring have been moved to our Corporate Unallocated segment.&#160;Prior period segment information has been recast retrospectively to reflect the realignment.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">The business components within each operating segment are managed to maximize the results of the overall operating segment rather than the results of any individual business component of the operating segment. Results of individual components of each operating segment are subject to numerous allocations of segment-wide costs that <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>or <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em><em style="font: inherit;">not</em> have been focused on that particular component for a particular reporting period. The costs for these allocated resources are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> tracked on a &#8220;where-used&#8221; basis as financial performance is assessed at the total operating segment level.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">Reportable operating segment financial information for all periods presented is as follows:</p>

   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">We use both GAAP and non-GAAP financial measures, including Adjusted EBITDA, for operational and financial decision making, and to assess Company and segment business performance. Adjusted EBITDA is <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> a measurement of financial performance under U.S. GAAP. Our calculation of this non-GAAP measure&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> may </em><em style="font: inherit;">not</em> be comparable to similarly titled measures of other companies due to potential differences between companies in the method of calculation. As a result, the use of this non-GAAP measure&#160;has limitations and should <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> be considered superior to, in isolation from, or as a substitute for, related U.S. GAAP measures.&#160;The following table provides a reconciliation of the Company&#8217;s Adjusted EBITDA to net income attributable to H.B. Fuller for the years ended <em style="font: inherit;"> November 29, 2025,&#160;</em><em style="font: inherit;"> November 30, 2024 </em>and <em style="font: inherit;"> December 2, 2023:</em></p>
